title: Homily II — Let us keep her feast in song and purity

edition.locus: Migne, PG 96 (Paris, 1860), Homily II on the Dormition, cols. 744-745 (PDF leaves 413-414)

source_text: Ταύτην ᾄσμασι ἱεροῖς εὐφημίσωμεν σήμερον, οἱ Χριστοῦ λαὸς καὶ εἶναι πεπλουτηκότες, καὶ λέγεσθαι. Ταύτην παννύχοις τιμήσωμεν στάσεσι· ταύτην ψυχῆς τε καὶ σώματος ἁγνότητι τέρψωμεν, τὴν ὄντως ἁγνὴν μετὰ Θεὸν ὑπὲρ ἅπαντας· πέφυκε γάρ πως τοῖς ὁμοίοις τὰ ὅμοια ἐπαγάλλεσθαι. Ταύτην ἐλέῳ καὶ συμπαθείᾳ τῶν ἐνδεῶν θεραπεύσωμεν. Εἰ γὰρ ἐπ' οὐδενὶ ὡς ἐλέῳ Θεὸς θεραπεύεται, τίς ἀντερεῖ μὴ τοῖς ἴσοις καὶ τὴν τούτου Μητέρα ἐπιφαιδρύνεσθαι; Αὕτη τὴν ἄφατον τῆς τοῦ Θεοῦ πρὸς ἡμᾶς ἀγάπης ἐδημοσίευσεν ἄβυσσον. Διὰ ταύτης ἡμῖν ὁ πρὸς τὸν Κτίστην πολυχρόνιος καταλέλυται πόλεμος. Διὰ ταύτης ἡμῖν αἱ πρὸς αὐτὸν καταλλαγαὶ ἐκροτήθησαν, καὶ εἰρήνη, καὶ χάρις δεδώρηται, καὶ ἀγγέλοις συγχορεύουσιν ἄνθρωποι, καὶ τέκνα Θεοῦ οἱ πρὶν ἠτιμημένοι κατέστημεν. Ἐκ ταύτης τὸν βότρυν τῆς ζωῆς ἐτρυγήσαμεν· ἐκ ταύτης τῆς ἀφθαρσίας τὸν βλαστὸν ἐδρεψάμεθα. Αὕτη πάντων τῶν ἀγαθῶν ἡμῖν προμνήστρια γέγονεν. Ἐν ταύτῃ ὁ Θεὸς μὲν ἄνθρωπος, καὶ Θεὸς ὁ ἄνθρωπος γέγονε. Καὶ τί τούτου παραδοξότερον; τί τούτου μακαριώτερον; Ἰλιγγιῶ τῷ φόβῳ, δεδιὼς τὸ λαλούμενον. Σὺν Μαριὰμ τῇ προφήτιδι, ὦ νεάνιδες ψυχαὶ, μετὰ τυμπάνων χορεύσωμεν, νεκροῦντες τὰ μέλη τὰ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς· τοῦτο γὰρ τὸ μυστικὸν τύμπανον· ἀλαλάξωμεν ἐπὶ τῆς κιβωτοῦ τοῦ Κυρίου τοῦ Θεοῦ ψυχῶν ἀλαλάγμασι, καὶ τείχη πεσοῦνται Ἱεριχούντια, τῶν ἐναντίων λέγω δυνάμεων τὰ δυσμενῆ ὀχυρώματα. Μετὰ Δαβὶδ σκιρτήσωμεν Πνεύματι· ἡ κιβωτὸς γὰρ Κυρίου σήμερον καταπέπαυται. Μετὰ Γαβριὴλ τοῦ τῶν ἀγγέλων πρωτοστάτου βοήσωμεν· Χαῖρε, κεχαριτωμένη, ὁ Κύριος μετὰ σοῦ. Χαῖρε, τὸ τῆς χαρᾶς ἀδαπάνητον πέλαγος. Χαῖρε, τὸ μόνον τῆς λύπης ἐξάλειπτρον. Χαίροις, πάσης καρδίας ἀκεσώδυνον φάρμακον. Χαίροις, δι' ἧς παρωθεῖται μὲν θάνατος, ἡ δὲ ζωὴ εἰσκεκόμισται.
pass_a_gloss: Her with sacred songs let us praise today, [we] the people (λαός) of Christ, who have been enriched both to be and to be called [so]. Her let us honour (τιμήσωμεν) with all-night (πάννυχος) standings. Her with purity (ἁγνότης) of soul and body let us delight (τέρψωμεν), the truly pure (ἁγνή) after God above all; for it is somehow natural (πέφυκε) for like things to exult in like. Her with mercy (ἔλεος) and compassion (συμπάθεια) for the needy (ἐνδεεῖς) let us serve/court. For if God is served by nothing as by mercy, who will gainsay (ἀντερεῖ) that his Mother too is brightened by the equal [things]? She published the unspeakable (ἄφατος) abyss (ἄβυσσος) of God's love (ἀγάπη) toward us. Through her the long-lasting war (πόλεμος) toward the Creator (Κτίστης) has been dissolved for us. Through her the reconciliations toward him were struck/ratified, and peace (εἰρήνη) and grace (χάρις) have been given, and men dance together with angels, and we, formerly dishonoured (ἠτιμημένοι), were made (κατέστημεν) children of God (τέκνα Θεοῦ). From her we harvested the cluster (βότρυς) of life; from her we plucked (ἐδρεψάμεθα) the shoot (βλαστός) of incorruption (ἀφθαρσία). She has become for us betrother/matchmaker of all good things. In her God has become man, and the man has become God. What more paradoxical than this? What more blessed? I am dizzy (ἰλιγγιῶ) with fear, dreading (δεδιώς) what is spoken. With Miriam (Μαριάμ) the prophetess, O young-maiden (νεάνιδες) souls, with timbrels (τύμπανα) let us dance, putting to death (νεκροῦντες) the members (μέλη) on earth; for this [is] the mystical (μυστικόν) timbrel. Let us shout (ἀλαλάξωμεν) at the ark (κιβωτός) of the Lord God with shouts (ἀλαλάγματα) of souls, and Jericho-walls will fall, I mean the hostile (δυσμενῆ) strongholds (ὀχυρώματα) of the opposing powers. With David let us leap in/by the Spirit (Πνεύματι); for the ark of the Lord today has come to rest. With Gabriel, the front-rank leader of the angels, let us cry: Rejoice (χαῖρε), graced one, the Lord [is] with you. Rejoice, the unspent (ἀδαπάνητον) sea (πέλαγος) of joy (χαρά). Rejoice, the only wiper-away of grief (λύπη). Rejoice (χαίροις), pain-healing (ἀκεσώδυνον) medicine (φάρμακον) of every heart. Rejoice, through whom death is thrust aside (παρωθεῖται) and life brought in.
pass_b_english: Let us praise her today with sacred songs, we who have been given the riches both of being and of being called the people of Christ. Let us honour her with vigils through the night. Let us delight her with purity of soul and body, her who after God is truly pure above all; and it is somehow natural for like to rejoice in like. Let us serve her with mercy and compassion for those in need. For if God is served by nothing so much as by mercy, who will deny that his Mother too is gladdened by the same?

She made known to all the unspeakable abyss of God's love for us. Through her the long war against the Creator has been ended for us. Through her our reconciliation with him was sealed, peace and grace have been given, human beings dance with angels, and we who before were dishonoured have become children of God. From her we gathered the cluster of life; from her we plucked the shoot of incorruption. She has become for us the go-between who brings us every good thing. In her God became man, and man became God. What is more astonishing than this? What more blessed? I grow dizzy with fear, in awe of what I am saying.

With Miriam the prophetess, O maiden souls, let us dance with timbrels (Exodus 15:20), putting to death our members that are on earth (Colossians 3:5); for this is the mystical timbrel. Let us raise a shout at the ark of the Lord God with the shouts of our souls, and the walls of Jericho will fall (Joshua 6:20), I mean the hostile strongholds of the opposing powers. With David let us leap in the Spirit (2 Samuel 6:14); for today the ark of the Lord has come to rest. With Gabriel, the first in rank among the angels, let us cry aloud: 'Rejoice, you who are full of grace; the Lord is with you' (Luke 1:28). Rejoice, inexhaustible sea of joy. Rejoice, you who alone wipe away sorrow. Rejoice, healing medicine for the pain of every heart. Rejoice, you through whom death is driven out and life is brought in.

choices.note: Margin refs checked against the wording: Exodus 15:20 (Miriam with timbrels); the margin prints 'Coloss. iii, 15', but νεκροῦντες τὰ μέλη τὰ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς is Colossians 3:5, cited so;
Joshua 6:20 (the walls fall at the shout);
'II Reg. 6:14' is 2 Kingdoms LXX = 2 Samuel 6:14 (David dancing before the ark);
Luke 1:28 (the greeting, rendered 'Rejoice, you who are full of grace' to match Homily I, section 1.7).
The 'mystical timbrel' rests on the drum being made of dead hide: putting the members to death is the drum the soul plays; kept as the author states it, without explanation.
'τὴν ὄντως ἁγνὴν μετὰ Θεὸν ὑπὲρ ἅπαντας' is in apposition, not a reason clause, so rendered 'her who after God is truly pure above all' (no 'for').
Allusions left uncited (general or uncertain): Hosea 6:6 / Matthew 9:13 behind 'God is served by nothing so much as by mercy';
John 1:12 or Romans 8:16 for 'children of God'; 2 Corinthians 10:4 for 'strongholds';
Psalm 132:8 for the ark coming to rest.
'θεραπεύω' (serve, pay court to) rendered 'serve' both times to keep the argument (if God is served by mercy, so is his Mother).
'προμνήστρια' is a marriage go-between; rendered 'the go-between who brings us every good thing'.
'Θεὸς ὁ ἄνθρωπος γέγονε' rendered 'man became God': the article points to the humanity God assumed in her, deified by the union; the English keeps the author's bare antithesis.
'ἐξάλειπτρον' (elsewhere 'unguent-box') is taken from ἐξαλείφω, 'wipe out', as the parallel requires: 'you who alone wipe away sorrow'.
'νεάνιδες ψυχαί' rendered 'maiden souls': νεᾶνις is a young woman, set in apposition to the souls, matching Miriam and the women with timbrels;
Psalm 68:25 (LXX 67:26, νεανίδων τυμπανιστριῶν, 'maidens playing timbrels') is a possible echo, left uncited.
'Πνεύματι' capitalised in the print and taken as the Holy Spirit.
